### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via retiredAfter (symbol, a field of const object pageActionBlockVariantDestructiveToDanger), retiredFromLoadPath (symbol, a field of const object pageActionBlockVariantDestructiveToDanger))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6817bf1eaebdc5a9856e019ce707b9bd9c244262` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `332bb6ce2ae81f5f68fa8260053fe4ab77894ed3` — the merge of head `2f05526d5ba495fd8845dbffc1470b3f9e30ee20` into base `6817bf1eaebdc5a9856e019ce707b9bd9c244262`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 332bb6ce2ae81f5f68fa8260053fe4ab77894ed3 && git checkout 332bb6ce2ae81f5f68fa8260053fe4ab77894ed3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6817bf1eaebdc5a9856e019ce707b9bd9c244262 2f05526d5ba495fd8845dbffc1470b3f9e30ee20 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6817bf1eaebdc5a9856e019ce707b9bd9c244262 && git merge --no-ff 2f05526d5ba495fd8845dbffc1470b3f9e30ee20

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6817bf1eaebdc5a9856e019ce707b9bd9c244262
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6817bf1eaebdc5a9856e019ce707b9bd9c244262` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Nothing below is a local re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The five rows move to `ACTION_BLOCK_VARIANTS`** (`default | danger | outline | secondary | ghost | link`, plus `primary` on `action:button`, `action:icon` and the group/menu member, exactly where it was): right. Triage 6448425754 rules the protocol spelling is `danger`, the word `ActionSchema.variant` (`action.zod.ts:1375`) and the runner (`ActionRunner.ts:1891`) read. `BUTTON_PRIMITIVE_VARIANTS` is module-private with the five readers the diff rewrites and none left in the tree, so replacing it rather than keeping it beside is right.
- **The refusal lives in the enum's error map, not in `aliases`**: right. `strictObject`'s `aliases` is a KEY table (`aliases[aliasProbe(key)]`, `strict-object.ts:32-34, 151`); a renamed VALUE has no key to alias. `actionBlockVariant()` keys the rename on `issue.input === 'destructive'` and returns `undefined` for every other miss, the `OBJECT_FORM_LAYOUT_RETIRED` / `FORM_VIEW_LAYOUT_RETIRED` shape (`component.zod.ts:6853`, `view.zod.ts:4449`). The claim's "aliases prescription" is met in substance: the refusal prescribes `danger` in so many words ("Write `variant: 'danger'`"), names the key the author wrote (`subject`), names the release ("in @objectstack/spec 18" — the pin's derivation for `retiredAfter` equal to the label, `retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts` header) and the chain step (`os migrate meta --from 17 --write`, `toMajor − 1`). The dev recorded the deviation in `out_of_scope_findings[1]`; judged right, no finding.
- **CONTROL rows**: an unknown value keeps the enum's own message and lists `"danger"`; pinned per row in the new test. Right.
- **D2 `page-action-block-variant-destructive-to-danger`** (`toMajor: 18`, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '18.2.0'`, order 77): right. `18.2.0` is the package label and the highest stamp on `main` was `18.1.0`, so the stamp is the newest published stable release and the pin's "every retired entry at the newest release has a JOIN row" guard is met by the six-refusal row added. Order 77 is free (76 is `main`'s highest) and the entry is inserted alphabetically. Reach is `mapPageComponents` (regions, slots single or list, nested through `mapComponentTree`, `walk.ts:403-460`), the props gate's own reach. It rewrites `properties.variant` on the four block types and member `variant` under `properties.actions` on the two containers only; `element:button` and every other value are left as stored; copy-on-write and idempotent by construction; fixture pair expects 6 notices over regions, a nested `page:card`, and a slotted header. Right.
- **D3 `ui-page-action-block-variant-destructive-refused`**: right. Both ids resolve where `check-adr-0087-registration` looks (`registry.ts` and the `entries/semantic` dir, script lines 511/527); both are added by this diff, so `registered` is the honest disposition. The generated `migrations/registry.ts` is gitignored and `check:generated` is reported 14/14 on the merged head.
- **ui renderers**: `toRunnerVariant` forwards `danger | primary | secondary | ghost | link` and nothing for `default` / `outline`; `toButtonVariant` draws `danger` as the primitive's `destructive`, `primary` as `default`, fallback otherwise. Four renderers draw through it; dropdown and menu items paint red on `danger`. `action-group.tsx:135` `toButtonVariant(action.variant || variant, 'outline')` is equivalent to the old chain because the group row never took `primary`. Registry `inputs` enums on `button` / `icon` list `danger`; `sdui.manifest.json` carries the two enum values; the record's `objectuiWorkspaceVersion` moves to the label. `runner-variant.ts` is not re-exported from the package index, so `toButtonVariant` / `ButtonPrimitiveVariant` widen no public surface. Right.
- **`UIActionSchema.variant`** stays by reference to `ActionButtonProps['variant']`, so it narrows with the row (`destructive` reds, `danger` accepted — the PR body's reverse check; the ui type-check is in progress). Right.
- **Forced edits** (`RecordDetailView.tsx` and `DetailView.tsx` Delete entry → `danger`; the `action-bar.tsx` doc example; the four fixtures): right — the menus now paint red on `danger` only. The page-header tests keep `variant: 'destructive'` on the host's `sys_delete` fixture as the by-name control (`containers.tsx:2281` reads `variant === 'danger' || name === 'sys_delete'`): right.
- **Public-surface changes implied**: `@objectstack/spec` `ComponentPropsMap` rows narrowed (value refused); `@object-ui/types` `UIActionSchema['variant']` narrowed by reference; `@object-ui/components` `toRunnerVariant` input narrowed (internal). No export renamed or removed. Right.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/26779-action-block-variant-danger.md`: `@objectstack/spec`, `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/types`, `@object-ui/plugin-detail` at `minor`. The kind is `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` (a value refused), and AGENTS.md step 3 says a kind takes at least `minor` on every package the diff moves, with `major` refused by `check-changeset-no-major`; `minor` is the level the rule yields for a narrowing. Right.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line-initial in the PR body and the changeset; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both; BREAKING banner; Before / Now / Fix; one marker `adr-0087: registered page-action-block-variant-destructive-to-danger, ui-page-action-block-variant-destructive-refused`; the prescription `**\`destructive\` → \`danger\`.**` is two backticked operands around an arrow, which `REWRITE_RE` (script line 1215) reads as a FROM → TO. Check Changeset, PR-body guards and Lint · CI, release & engine gates are `success`. Right.
- **`@object-ui/app-shell` absent from the frontmatter**: not owed. The package is `private: true` and left the Changesets `fixed` group at #25922 (`.changeset/25922-unpublish-app-shell.md`: "`18.2.0` is the last published `@object-ui/app-shell`"); step 3 owes a changeset to "anything that publishes", and this package publishes nothing. Neither must-fix nor should-fix.
- **The unreleased `.changeset/26665-action-block-destructive-confirm.md` on `main`**: should-fix, in this PR. It compiles into the same `@object-ui/components` / `@object-ui/types` CHANGELOG entry as this one and says the blocks translate `destructive` to `danger` and that "`danger` stays refused there" — both untrue once this PR lands, in the same release. AGENTS.md row 708 lets a released CHANGELOG entry be corrected only by a dedicated docs-only PR afterwards, so the cheap moment is before the release consumes the file: trim the sentence that describes the removed bridge (or note that #26779 supersedes it) in this PR. Not a must-fix: the contract and this PR's own changeset carry the truth; only release prose is stale.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared.
- `out_of_scope_findings[0]` (the #26665 changeset): answered above as should-fix here, not left for the seat.
- `out_of_scope_findings[1]` (the `aliases` wording): answered in ① — the deviation is right.
- PR body "Not measurable from here: stored deployed rows and hotcrm sources": stored rows are measured by code, not by deployment (④ below). A hotcrm source with a `destructive` block meets `validateComponentProps` as a gating `error` on `os validate`, `os build` and `os lint` (`authoring-rules.ts:1264-1288`, `AUTHORING_COMMANDS = ['validate','build','lint']`) and the enum's rename at the runtime save door (`surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['page']`). Accepted.
- PR body "Unchanged on purpose" (page-header fixtures, `ActionPreview.tsx`): read in the cited code; both hold.
- Dogfood: the two failures in `packaged-action-disabled-dispatch-live.dogfood.test.ts` are the recorded load flake, this diff touches no action-disable path, and the head's Dogfood Regression Gate is `success`. Accepted.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay note owed.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing is judged against the published spec on `main` (`8074feb6` as first read; `aa00362f` merge-base): the spec declares a destructive action block and keeps declaring it, now under the one spelling `danger`. The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real at every door rather than taking a capability away at the consumer, so it is the right kind of narrowing under Prime Directive 12. The #26776 bridge existed only because the spec spoke two dialects; with one dialect the bridge is exactly the "lenient alias in a consumer" that directive forbids, so removing it is right **provided** no stored page reaches a renderer with `destructive`. I tried to break that claim path by path:

1. **Stored `page` rows** — `DatabaseLoader.rowToData` (`database-loader.ts:884`), the protocol's `convertStoredItem` (`getMetaItems`, `loadMetaFromDb`, drafts; `protocol.ts:7334, 9835, 10880, 10945`) and `ObjectQLPlugin.convertStoredRow` (`plugin.ts:3115`) all go through `applyConversionsToStoredItem`, which pins `includeRetired: true` (`stored.ts`). The new test replays that seam over a stored page row for all four blocks and a member and parses the result against the row that now refuses `destructive`. Covered.
2. **Built artifacts and package install** — `applyArtifactForwardConversions` (metadata plugin door, engine, `load-artifact-bundle`, `app-plugin`) opens the window per entry: `floor < runtime OR floor ≤ retiredAfter OR (floor = M.0.0 AND toMajor = M)`. With `retiredAfter: '18.2.0'` equal to the running label, every artifact declaring a floor at or below 18.2.0 (including `^18` and `^18.2.0`) replays; a floor above 18.2.0 can only be built by a spec that already refuses the value. Covered.
3. **Sources** — `os migrate meta --from 17 --write` reaches the entry by id through the chain; the prescription names it. Covered.
4. **History rows** are served verbatim by design; a restore goes through the save door and meets the rename loudly. Acceptable.
5. **Authored sources on the load path** (`defineStack` / the fs loader at `os dev`): a page's `properties` is not parsed there, and the authoring funnel never replays a retired entry, so a stale source draws the fallback variant with a neutral confirm until `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` refuse it. This is not a stored page and is the posture every `retiredFromLoadPath` page entry on `main` already takes (`page-action-row-navigation-executor-to-url`, `page-template-full-width-to-default`, …); the D3 entry states it. Read, not a finding.
6. **ui packages that parse pages themselves** — `ui/packages/types/src/zod/*` carries no action-block variant list (its `destructive` enums are badge, alert, toast and button-group primitives); `DeclaredActionsBar`, `record-quick-actions`, `MetadataTypeActions`, `elements.tsx` already map the ActionSchema's `danger` onto the primitive's `destructive`, consistent with the new dialect. One stale duplicate remains: `ui/packages/vscode-extension/src/providers/SchemaValidator.ts:234-239` validates a `button` node's `variant` against a hand-copied `default | destructive | outline | secondary | ghost | link` (it already lacked `primary`), so if that `button` is the action block it now warns on the canonical `danger` and accepts the refused `destructive`. **Should-fix**: read the vocabulary from the spec row or drop the check; a warning-severity diagnostic in a private editor extension, no render path.

No path lets a stored page carry `destructive` to a renderer, so the bridge removal is not a must-fix. The conversion's own docblock reads the seams correctly. Findings: two should-fix (②'s unreleased #26665 changeset, ④'s vscode validator list), no must-fix.

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [40648482070](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/40648482070) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Test UI (11/16)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/40648482070/job/122684573732)** — 失败步骤: Run the ui tests (shard 11/16)

  ```
  × (f) CONTROL: offers it, once, to a member granted that permission 55ms
  FAIL   dom  packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/AppReportIndex.navGates-26892.test.tsx > ⌘K offers its navigation entries as the sidebar shows them (objectstack#26892) > (f) CONTROL: offers it, onc
    ↳ 失败原因: AssertionError: expected [ 'Alpha', 'Beta', 'Gamma' ] to deeply equal [ 'Alpha', 'Beta', 'Delta', 'Gamma' ]
  ```

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
